Asha R: quick heads-up — ran a full nsys capture on the KV cache hotpath and most CUDA kernels show up but none of the Python/C++ frames have line info. stack frames are just module+offset. anyone seen this when running inside our distroless-ish runtime with overlay mounts?

Ben T: hmm yeah that sounds like missing debug symbols or build flags. what command did you run?

Asha R: `nsys profile --output=kvcache-run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt python -m myserving.benchmark --iters 200`

Asha R: repro notes: image is based on our runtime: `redwood/runtime:prod-2026-03`, we mount /host/usr/lib/cuda readonly into `/usr/local/cuda` for compatibility, and we use distroless python.

Kunal P: two quick things to check: 1) CUPTI (and libcupti.so) must be visible inside the container at the expected path; nsys falls back silently sometimes. 2) were binaries built with `-g` and without `-fno-omit-frame-pointer`?

Jia L: also check if overlayfs pathmap is rewriting build-ids. `nsys` resolves addresses to lineinfo via ELF build-ids and debuglink; if you copy or mount libs at different paths it can fail to match.

Asha R: libcupti.so is present at `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` inside the container. `ldd` shows it linked. I still get entries like `myserving.so+0x1f3a7` with no source.

Ben T: can you paste `readelf -n myserving.so | grep GNU` and `eu-readelf -n`? also `file myserving.so` to check if it's stripped.

Asha R: `file myserving.so: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), not stripped`

Asha R: `readelf -n myserving.so` shows an NT_GNU_BUILD_ID present.

Kunal P: ok so not stripped. Next guess: nsys may be resolving but the UI (or the `nsys stats` export) might be missing inlined frame mapping because debug info is in a separate .debug file not present. Do you have separate debug packages?

Asha R: we don't ship .debug files in prod images. but i expected at least function names and file:line if symbols exist in the .so.

Jia L: another angle — CUPTI/Nsight sometimes needs `NSYS_UI=1` or the `--force` option to regenerate symbol cache. try `nsys profile --force --output=kvcache-run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt ...`

Ben T: also try running `nsys export --report=timeline kvcache-run1.qdrep` and then `nsys stats --report=cupti kvcache-run1.qdrep` to see if the raw metrics have kernel names. If metrics have kernel names but timeline UI lacks lines it's prob mapping issue.

Asha R: ran export+stats, kernels listed as `kernel_unnamed` in the timeline. `nsys reporter` shows offsets only.

Kunal P: FYI we've hit this when the container's `/proc` is a host overlay and `nsys` can't read `/proc/<pid>/maps` correctly. It reads mapping with host indices and then fails to find debug files. Can you run `cat /proc/self/maps` inside the container and compare to host?

Asha R: `infra-bot` dug out a CI run that reproduced it — attaching small excerpt: `proc maps show /usr/local/cuda/lib64 -> /host/usr/local/cuda/lib64 (overlay)`.

infra-bot: CI run 2026-03-10T12:04 produced `kvcache-run1.qdrep` attached to job 1182.

Jia L: overlay remapping is almost certainly it. Options: 1) bind-mount libs to the same absolute path as inside the host so `nsys` resolves; 2) run nsys with `--trace-children` and make sure the process namespace is not interfering; 3) copy debug symbols into container image.

Ben T: practical quick test: run the same workload on a non-overlay image (temporary vanilla cuda image) and see if lineinfo appears. If yes, then it's an overlay/mount resolution problem.

Asha R: ran on `nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime` and lineinfo shows up as expected. so overlay rotation is definitely the culprit.

Kunal P: sweet. Two follow-ups: - file a short repro that our infra team can run (you already have qdrep). - for production images we should consider shipping a minimal `.debug` tarball for internal perf ops so we don't need host libs. Could be toggled by env var at runtime.

Jia L: also consider setting `NSYS_USE_CUPTI_API=0` as a test (forces a different collection path) — might give hints.

Asha R: logged a ticket: PERF-4827 with qdrep and steps. Plan: pair with infra on Tuesday, try `--force`/copy debug files, and add CI smoke that runs an `nsys` export step to catch regressions.

Ben T: nice. add a short note in eng-runtime README about how overlay mounts can break symbol resolution and the quick debug checklist: check libcupti, compare /proc maps, try non-overlay image.

Asha R: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
